description: Which version a forge tag names, so a consumer can list a project's releases from tags alone. `expect` is the version, or null when the tag names none and the release is reachable only through a signed release list. The packslip inside the release remains the authority.

cases.name: the common spelling
no leading v
calver is semver
a two-component tag normalizes
leading zeros normalize
a prerelease part survives
the repository name may prefix the tag
a monorepo subpath may prefix it
the last segment of a subpath may prefix it
an @ separator counts
a prefix that leaves no version does not end the search
cases.comment: The subpath tool- begins the tag but leaves suite-1.2.0; the repository name tool-suite- leaves 1.2.0.

cases.name: the subpath still prefixes the tool's own tags
the first prefix that leaves a version wins
cases.comment: Prefixes are tried in order: subpath, last subpath segment, repository name, then none. The subpath tool- leaves 2.0-1.0.0, which is 2.0.0-1.0.0, before the longer repository name tool-2.0- is tried.

cases.name: the repository name prefixes the tag in any case
cases.comment: GitHub resolves jqlang/JQ as jqlang/jq, so a request in another case lists the same tags.

cases.name: a subpath prefixes the tag only in its own case
cases.comment: A monorepo subpath names a tool, not a forge name, so it compares exactly.

cases.name: a tag naming no version is skipped
another project's prefix is not this project's
a date is not a version tag for this project
a dotted date drops its leading zeros
a dashed date names no version
cases.comment: Consumers do not respell dashed dates. The vendor signs 2026.8.31 and maps this tag in a signed list, or tags the release v2026.08.31.
